hyps.why: With node 1 dead, a conv on edge 4 has no input, so the edit does nothing.
Edge 2 has no input when node 1 is dead, so its conv is wasted.
Node 2 cannot reach the output when edge 5 is none, so a conv on edge 1 is wasted.
A conv on edge 2 is useless when node 2 has no outgoing edge to the output.
With node 1 dead, removing edge 4 changes nothing, so it is less harmful than when edge 0 is active.
Edge 2 carries no signal when node 1 is dead, so cutting it costs nothing.
Edge 1 only feeds the output through edge 5, so removing it is harmless when edge 5 is none.
Replacing none with a conv adds a whole new path to the output, a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
Replacing a useful direct skip with conv gives less gain, or even loses the residual benefit.
Turning an empty edge into a conv adds capacity that is not there when the edge already has an op.
